== EXTRACTION RULES (GEMINI_HANDOFF_BRIEF §3 Task C & §5.2; CODEBOOK.md §§1-9; RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1) ==

NEVER copy publication year or country from the citation header when the full paper was not read!
2. IF FULL TEXT IS READABLE:
   - Extract each of the 9 fields strictly from the paper text. Write a field value ONLY if the paper explicitly states it; if not stated in the paper, write `"not reported"` in `value` and explain in `comment`. Never guess or infer from context.
   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.
   - `country`: Country or countries studied as stated in the paper (use semicolon-separated names if multiple specific countries, or exact global/regional scope as stated, e.g. `"Global (48 countries)"`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).
   - `outcome_flags`: Comma-separated list using ONLY exact `CODEBOOK.md` §5 codes actually studied in the paper (`formal_connection`, `water_access`, `sanitation_access`, `service_coverage`, `service_reliability`, `service_quantity`, `service_quality`, `affordability`, `service_continuity`, `application_success`, `refusal`, `delay`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `mechanism_flags`: Comma-separated list of applicable top-level family codes (`ELIGIBILITY`, `BURDEN`, `DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION`, `ENFORCEMENT`) followed by exact detailed `CODEBOOK.md` §4 codes actually studied in the paper (`documentation`, `tenure`, `property`, `planning`, `zoning`, `building_permit`, `service_area`, `fees`, `procedural_steps`, `delay`, `discretion`, `hardship_exception`, `accommodation`, `administrative_review`, `complaint`, `judicial_review`, `disconnection`, `reconnection`, `sanction`, `participation`, `institutional_fragmentation`, `political_coordination`, `bureaucratic_assistance`), or `"not reported"`.
3. `where_found` AND `evidence_quotes`:
   - Every field's `where_found` must give exact PDF page(s), section, and/or table/figure number (e.g. `"PDF p. 4, Section 2.2; Table 1, PDF p. 7"`).

country.comment: Trial conducted in rural villages across four provinces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (Kongo Central, Kasai, Kasai Central, and South Kivu; North Kivu was excluded prior to trial launch due to logistical infeasibility with only 3 clusters).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF pp. 4-5, Methods (Study design and participants)

effect_estimate.comment: At median 3.6 years post-intervention, the community-driven WASH program significantly increased local WASH governance institutions, self-reported improved water and sanitation access, water governance satisfaction, likelihood of paying for water, and water-point microbial quality slightly, while water-point functionality was lower and there were null effects on child diarrhea, length-for-age Z-score, household stored water quality, and water collection time.
effect_estimate.value: Intention-to-treat linear regression at 3.6-year follow-up: WASH institutions index +0.40 SD (95% CI 0.16 to 0.65; n = 329 villages) and active WASH/water committee +21 percentage points (pp); household use of an improved water source +24 pp (95% CI 12 to 36); household use of an improved sanitation facility +18 pp (95% CI 10 to 25); positive perceptions of water governance +0.19 SD (95% CI 0.04 to 0.34), driven by satisfaction with water access (+0.56 points on 1-5 scale, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.85); paying for water +9 pp (95% CI 0 to 19; no difference in amount paid conditional on paying, and no effect on collection time); observed water-point functionality -11 pp (95% CI -0.18 to -0.05; 85% intervention vs. 97% control); water-point thermotolerant coliforms -0.17 log10(MPN)/100 mL (95% CI -0.32 to -0.02; no difference in household stored water). Null effects on child 7-day diarrhea prevalence (adjusted mean difference -0.01, 95% CI -0.05 to 0.03; n = 4,072 children) and child length-for-age Z-score (adjusted mean difference -0.01, 95% CI -0.15 to 0.12; n = 2,142 children).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 1-2, Abstract; PDF pp. 8-12, Results and Table 3

mechanism_certainty.comment: Pre-registered cluster-randomized controlled trial (appraised with RoB 2 cluster-randomized trials variant) experimentally evaluating a national community-driven WASH intervention that created elected village WASH committees, community action/maintenance plans, and Health Zone bureaucratic support alongside infrastructure grants ($2,000 water, $2,000 sanitation) and behavior change campaigns, directly measuring institutional persistence and WASH access at 3.6 years. Note that institutional strengthening is bundled with capital subsidies and behavior change, and participants/interviewers were unmasked with no baseline survey.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 4-8, Methods; PDF pp. 8-11, Results and Table 3

mechanism_flags.comment: The intervention ('Healthy Villages' component of DRC's Healthy Villages and Schools program) operates through community participation and self-governance (electing a village WASH committee, community action and maintenance plans, collective decision-making), bureaucratic and NGO assistance (3-6 months of Health Zone/Health Area official and NGO support, volunteer training, monthly/weekly supervisory visits, and financing), multi-step formal administrative certification procedures (9 program steps including formal request, signed agreement with the Health Zone, KAP assessments, and Chief Medical Officer certification), and local water fee/petty cash management.

outcome_flags.comment: Measured outcomes include household use of improved water sources and time spent collecting water (water_access), use of improved sanitation facilities (sanitation_access), microbial water quality via E. coli/thermotolerant coliform MPN testing at water points and household storage containers (service_quality), directly observed water-point functionality and reported breakdown duration (service_reliability), and whether households pay for water and amount paid (affordability).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 6-7, Methods (Outcomes); PDF pp. 10-12, Results

risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF pp. 4-5, Methods (Study design and participants, Randomization and masking)

sample_size.comment: 339 eligible villages in 121 clusters were randomized, and 7 villages were dropped to meet operational targets/coding error, leaving 332 villages in 121 clusters (50 intervention clusters / 146 villages; 71 control clusters / 186 villages). At the 3.6-year follow-up, 3,283 households (1,438 intervention, 1,845 control) were interviewed across 329 villages. Primary outcomes analyzed 4,072 children under 5 for diarrhea (1,762 intervention, 2,310 control across 2,466 households), 2,142 children under 5 for length-for-age Z-score (919 intervention, 1,223 control), and 329 villages for the WASH institutions index (144 intervention, 185 control).

study_design.comment: Parallel cluster-randomized controlled trial stratified by province and number of villages per cluster (12 randomization blocks), analyzed on an intention-to-treat basis using linear models with stratum fixed effects and cluster-robust standard errors at median 3.6 years post-intervention (without baseline survey).
study_design.value: Cluster-randomized controlled trial (stratified block randomization across 12 strata with intention-to-treat linear regression at median 3.6-year follow-up)
